title: Tag Source Data
content_html:
Tag Source Data

Canonical Owners

All four sources live under studio/data/canonical/tags/.

Source Owns Why separate
tag-registry.json flat canonical tag identity, one scalar group, ordered document-location references, allowed-group policy classification and references can change without changing tag identity
tag-aliases.json shorthand keys and canonical tag targets alias curation can evolve independently of canonical identity
tag-assignments.json series tags and nested per-work override deltas assignment state changes independently of vocabulary
tag-groups.json ordered descriptive taxonomy prose explanatory content is not registry or assignment state

The exact schemas and limits are enforced by studio/services/tags/tag_source_model.py; the JSON files are current data, not documentation examples.

Relationship Model

tag-groups descriptions
        |
tag-registry canonical IDs + group + doc_url[]
        ^
tag-aliases shorthand targets
        |
tag-assignments series rows
        -> nested work override deltas
        -> public series/work membership indexes

registry doc_url[]
        -> zero or more canonical public document placements
        -> documents remain independently owned

Durable rules:

  • registry IDs are globally unique slug-safe names; each row has exactly one independently validated scalar group;
  • registry rows use tag_registry_v5 and contain exactly tag_id, group, doc_url, and updated_at_utc; consumers display tag_id, and there is no registry-row label or description;
  • doc_url is an ordered array. An empty array is a valid unlinked state; exact URLs cannot repeat within one row, but several tags may reference the same URL;
  • supported values are canonical root-relative Analysis or configured /docs/ routes. They contain no origin, fragment, or incidental viewer state;
  • URL identity preserves placement context. One source document may therefore appear through more than one report URL;
  • a stored URL may become unavailable. It remains canonical source data until an explicit edit removes it; no title or current UI context repairs it;
  • documents contain no tag back-reference. Tag and document group, title, content, and lifecycle remain independent after any creation-time seed;
  • aliases and assignments store flat canonical IDs;
  • alias targets must be canonical tags and may not duplicate a registry- resolved group within one alias;
  • a work override belongs under one series row, not in a global work table;
  • effective work tags combine series tags with the override delta;
  • an override that duplicates a series tag is removed during normalization;
  • series/work membership comes from public catalogue indexes and remains externally owned.

Write Boundary

The browser reads and writes through the allowlisted /studio/api/tags/... boundary. Mutation planners validate cross-file effects before studio/services/tags/tag_write_transactions.py atomically replaces one or more canonical files.

tag-groups.json is currently read-only through the app. Registry, aliases, and assignments are writable.

New Tag validates its submitted tag and destination, creates one Analysis tags source document, stores that document's canonical published placement at doc_url[0], rebuilds the exact child projection, and records the action as one transaction. It does not audit, deduplicate, or repair other rows.

Edit Tag submits the immutable tag_id, accepted scalar group, and complete ordered doc_url[]. The write validates supported URL shape and within-row duplicates, but not current document-location-provider membership: a selected location may become unavailable before Save and stale references must remain removable. Delete removes the tag and its accepted alias/assignment effects; it never deletes a referenced document.

The title picker and Registry presentation read the compact public document-location projections. Those projections are rebuilt from published search/report/sub-scope data during the owning publication flow; unpublished source or manage-only data is not an authoring option.

Change Method

  • vocabulary change: start with Registry/Aliases planners and inspect assignment effects;
  • assignment change: preserve series-first ownership and validate catalogue membership;
  • registry location change: preserve exact URL order and identity; do not infer a replacement from title, selected parent, displayed document, or another placement;
  • schema change: update loaders, focused mutation paths, migrations, audits, public location projections, and focused tests;
  • catalogue membership change: use the Studio catalogue synchronization path, then run the narrow consistency check.

Weak Spots

  • cross-file referential integrity is enforced in services/audits rather than by one transactional database;
  • assignment validity depends on generated public catalogue indexes;
  • aliases can preserve historical selection context in assignments, creating a subtle dependency even after canonical IDs are resolved;
  • deleting or unpublishing a document does not update tag-registry.json; unavailable URLs remain until an explicit tag edit;
  • URL validation proves canonical supported shape, not live provider membership or continued resolution;
  • Studio currently offers an Analysis-only link picker and no bulk repair, reorder, or Studio association UI;
  • hand-editing JSON bypasses planners and activity records.

Site Consistency Audit is the cross-boundary check. Focused schema behaviour lives in the tag service tests.
